basic_information.short_title: Continued Use of Funds for Unpaid Obligations, FY2020–2022
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CONTINUED USE OF FUNDS FOR THE RELEASE AND DISBURSEMENT OF UNPAID OBLIGATIONS OF FY 2020, 2021, AND 2022 APPROPRIATIONS
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: Immediately after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Lets the region keep paying old bills. Money already committed under the 2020, 2021 and 2022 budgets stays effective until it is fully released and disbursed — with no closing date.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: Obligations had been entered into under three budget years but not yet paid, and the appropriations backing them were expiring. Rather than leave contractors and suppliers unpaid, Parliament kept the money effective.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: For each of the 3 years, infrastructure, capital outlays and operating programmes obligated by the stated cut-off remain effective until fully released and disbursed. Personnel Services still expires on its original date each year.
who_will_be_affected: Contractors and suppliers owed money on completed work
Communities whose projects were funded but unpaid
Constituent LGUs, whose share of income taxes stays available until fully expended
Bangsamoro ministries and offices carrying unpaid obligations
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: Took effect immediately on publication in June 2023.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. Bills already incurred under the 2020, 2021 and 2022 budgets can still be paid — the appropriations stay effective until fully released and disbursed, with no end date. Salaries are still excluded.
in_practice: FY2020: infrastructure, capital outlays and continuing MOOE programmes obligable to 31 December 2022, and the appropriation continues to be effective until fully released and disbursed
FY2021: the same, obligable to 31 December 2022
FY2022: infrastructure, capital outlays and Support to Operations and Operations under MOOE obligable to 31 December 2023, and effective until fully released and disbursed
Personnel Services expires on its original date for each year — 2020, 2021 and 2022 respectively
General Administration and Support MOOE is excluded for FY2022
Constituent LGUs' share of income taxes collected in the BARMM stays available until fully expended or disbursed

for_specific_groups.Contractors and suppliers: If work was completed and obligated under any of these three budgets, the money to pay you does not lapse on a date.
for_specific_groups.Local government units: Your share of income taxes collected in the region is available until fully expended or disbursed.
for_specific_groups.Government employees: Nothing changes — salary appropriations expire on their original dates in every year.

what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: In force since June 2023, with no closing date on the disbursement of obligated amounts.
what_you_can_do: If you are owed for completed work under one of these budgets, the appropriation backing it remains effective
Read alongside BAA 14, 24 and 33, the earlier extensions of the same budgets
watch_out_for: This is where the open-ended wording enters the general budget: obligated appropriations continue 'until fully released and disbursed', with no final date.
It applies only to amounts already obligated by the stated cut-offs — it does not let new commitments be made indefinitely.
No reporting requirement attaches to the extended amounts.

key_terms_explained.GAS: General Administration and Support — the overhead category excluded for FY2022.

benefits.headline: Old bills can still be paid — obligated money stays effective until fully disbursed.

direct_benefits.benefit: Payment for completed work funded under the 2020–2022 budgets
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Contractors, suppliers and the communities awaiting the works

direct_benefits.benefit: LGU shares of income taxes available until fully expended
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Stated in the amended FY2022 provision

indirect_benefits: Avoids leaving contractors unpaid for work already accepted
limitations: No end date on disbursement, and no reporting attached.

for_citizens: None. The act governs government spending.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management (MFBM), authorised to issue the implementing guidelines
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A contractor completed a school building funded in the 2021 budget but was not paid before the appropriation was due to lapse. Under this act the appropriation remains effective until fully released and disbursed.
An agency with unspent 2022 salary money cannot carry it forward — Personnel Services expired at the end of 2022.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Further amends Section 47 of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 3 (FY2020). Appropriations are available for release and disbursement until 31 December 2022 except as provided; infrastructure, capital outlays and continuing programmes under MOOE are valid for obligation until 31 December 2022, and the appropriation continues to be effective until fully released and disbursed. Personnel Services remains valid only until 31 December 2020.

Section 2 — Further amends Section 47 of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 15 (FY2021) in parallel terms, with obligation to 31 December 2022 and the appropriation continuing to be effective until fully released and disbursed. Personnel Services remains valid until 31 December 2021.

Section 3 — Further amends Section 48 of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 23 (FY2022). All appropriations except Personnel Services and General Administration and Support under MOOE are available for release and disbursement until the periods specified, while the amount appropriated as the constituent LGUs' share of income taxes collected within the BARMM is available until fully expended or disbursed. Infrastructure, capital outlays, and Support to Operations and Operations under MOOE are valid for obligation until 31 December 2023, and the appropriation continues to be effective until fully released and disbursed. Personnel Services remains valid only until 31 December 2022.
Section 6 — Takes effect immediately after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation.

who_benefits: Contractors and suppliers owed for completed work
impact.allocated_budget: No new appropriation. It keeps effective the appropriations of BAA 3 (FY2020), BAA 15 (FY2021) and BAA 23 (FY2022).
impact.figures_note: The act states no amount — it changes the conditions under which existing appropriations remain effective.

related_legislation.related_note: The third act to extend the FY2020 budget, after BAA 14 and BAA 24. It is the point at which the phrase 'until fully released and disbursed' enters the general appropriations — 6 months before BAA 51 applied comparable wording to the Special Development Fund.

citizen_questions.a: Paying bills already incurred. For the 2020, 2021 and 2022 budgets, amounts obligated by the stated cut-off dates remain effective until fully released and disbursed.

citizen_questions.q: Is there a final deadline to pay?
citizen_questions.a: No. That is the significant part — once obligated, the appropriation continues to be effective until fully released and disbursed, with no closing date.

citizen_questions.q: Can new commitments still be made?
citizen_questions.a: No. The obligation deadlines were 31 December 2022 for the 2020 and 2021 budgets and 31 December 2023 for 2022. Only payment of what was already obligated continues.
No. Personnel Services expires on its original date in each of the 3 years.
